title: Steve Jobs's emails to himself (2003): what moved him in music, and how he saw Pixar's Golden Age
summary: Two private notes Jobs wrote in 2003: a playlist writeup about songs that made him cry or recalled his childhood, and talk prep celebrating Pixar's Golden Age. They show his taste, emotional honesty, and view that great work comes from the maturing of people.

principles.text: Pixar's greatness was fueled by people growing into mastery, not by any single product.
principles.quote: Our real Golden Age is being fueled by the maturing of our people.

principles.text: Celebrate a track record of original work, and judge success against the history of the field.
principles.quote: All original Pixar stories. Our track record of 4 for 4, and hopefully 5 for 5, is unparalleled in the history of animation, and indeed in the history of film.

principles.text: Build a bench: watch for the next generation of leaders coming up behind the current one.
principles.quote: And I see more directors and producers coming right behind them.

principles.text: Pause to recognize that you are living through a great moment while it is happening.
principles.quote: Tonight is a night for celebration, but don’t forget to pause for a moment and realize that this is what it feels like to be living in—and creating—a Golden Age.

principles.text: Great art connects to personal, emotional truth; his taste was guided by what moved him deeply.
principles.quote: Maybe it’s because I’m adopted, but this song moves me like few others.

principles.text: Technology and the arts meet through craft: lyrics and music he loved shaped his sense of quality.
principles.quote: I had not listened to much Jackson Browne at that time, and was just blown away by the lyrics.
